```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)

root_dir <- normalizePath("..")
load(file.path(root_dir, "data", "bangaloreRainfall.RData"))
```

## Question

`r rmarkdown::metadata$question`

This is a source-choice check for the daily rain chart, not a climate finding.
Compare September 1–27, the latest complete days shared by the local WeatherUnion
snapshot and the Oikolab archive. One Oikolab point is compared with separate
station totals; the station median is a description of the sampled localities,
not an estimate of a single citywide gauge. Count only stations with all 648
hours and 648 valid derived rainfall measurements. The case for using the older
GFS values would weaken if the station totals were near the current Oikolab
total, or if missing station hours explained the difference. Old GFS hourly
values would be needed to reproduce the earlier chart exactly. Oikolab's
archived 00Z runs allow a separate GFS reconstruction.

## First, check the stored Oikolab source window

The updater groups `DT` into dates with `as.Date(DT)`, which uses UTC for this
POSIXct object. Here the comparison is a complete September 1–27 IST window;
the site CSV is checked separately because it now uses the GFS override.

```{r oikolab-coverage}
start_ist <- as.POSIXct("2026-09-01", tz = "Asia/Kolkata")
end_ist <- as.POSIXct("2026-09-28", tz = "Asia/Kolkata")

blrRain %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(
    hour_ist = as.POSIXct(
      format(DT, tz = "Asia/Kolkata", usetz = FALSE),
      tz = "Asia/Kolkata"
    ),
    rain_mm = as.numeric(Rain)
  ) %>%
  filter(hour_ist >= start_ist, hour_ist < end_ist) ->
  oikolab_september

oikolab_september %>%
  summarise(
    hours = n(),
    expected_hours = 27 * 24,
    duplicate_hours = sum(duplicated(hour_ist)),
    missing_rain = sum(is.na(rain_mm)),
    rain_mm = sum(rain_mm),
    .by = Source
  )

read_csv(
  file.path(root_dir, "docs", "data", "bangalore_daily_weather.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  filter(
    DT >= as.Date("2026-09-01"),
    DT <= as.Date("2026-09-27")
  ) %>%
  summarise(days = n(), rain_mm = sum(Rain))
```

## Now compare complete WeatherUnion stations

`rain_mm` is derived from station accumulation changes. Missing hours are not
treated as dry. Keep the point series and the station distribution separate.

```{r weatherunion-coverage}
open_dataset(
  file.path(root_dir, "data", "weatherunion_bengaluru_hourly.parquet")
) %>%
  filter(hour_ist >= start_ist, hour_ist < end_ist) %>%
  summarise(
    hours = n(),
    valid_rain_hours = sum(!is.na(rain_mm)),
    rain_mm = sum(rain_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = c(locality_id, current_locality_name)
  ) %>%
  collect() ->
  station_totals

station_totals %>%
  count(hours, valid_rain_hours, sort = TRUE)

station_totals %>%
  filter(hours == 648, valid_rain_hours == 648) ->
  complete_stations

complete_stations %>%
  summarise(
    stations = n(),
    min_mm = min(rain_mm),
    median_mm = median(rain_mm),
    max_mm = max(rain_mm)
  )
```

The September 23 archived chart covered data through September 22. Check that
cutoff separately before comparing its rounded 90 mm label.

```{r archived-chart-cutoff}
open_dataset(
  file.path(root_dir, "data", "weatherunion_bengaluru_hourly.parquet")
) %>%
  filter(
    hour_ist >= start_ist,
    hour_ist < as.POSIXct("2026-09-23", tz = "Asia/Kolkata")
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    hours = n(),
    valid_rain_hours = sum(!is.na(rain_mm)),
    rain_mm = sum(rain_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = locality_id
  ) %>%
  collect() %>%
  filter(hours == 22 * 24, valid_rain_hours == 22 * 24) %>%
  summarise(stations = n(), median_mm = median(rain_mm))
```

The complete stations' September 1–27 totals range from 55.6 to 154.2 mm,
with a median of 95.6 mm. After the September 29 daily refresh, the stored
Oikolab archive totals 25.71 mm for the same window (22.82 mm ERA5, 2.89 mm
GFS). Before the override, the September 28 site CSV reported 22.65 mm
through September 27. WeatherUnion therefore gives strong evidence that the
earlier rain chart was unrepresentative of these observed localities. It does
not establish that every
ERA5 variable is wrong or that the old GFS forecasts were accurate by day.

## Can we use an archived GFS series?

The [earlier audit](september-rain-revisions.html) found that the archived chart
label was 90 mm on September 23, 62 mm on September 25, and 23 mm on September
28. The September 1–22 WeatherUnion median is 95.6 mm, close to the first
rounded chart label, though daily rain and observation sites differ. The update
job replaces older GFS hours with ERA5 and overwrites the RData; it keeps no
hourly revision history. Archived PNGs preserve rounded labels, not the exact
old hourly values. But Oikolab's `/archivedforecast` endpoint retains 00Z GFS
runs. I fetched 29 runs (August 31 through September 28), selected forecast
lead hours 1–24 from each, and saved them with cycle and lead-hour provenance
in `data/oikolab_gfs_00z_2026-09.csv`.
This is a consistent reconstruction, not the exact earlier chart series.

```{r archived-gfs}
read_csv(
  file.path(root_dir, "data", "oikolab_gfs_00z_2026-09.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  mutate(
    hour_utc = as.POSIXct(
      hour_utc,
      format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ",
      tz = "UTC"
    ),
    hour_ist = as.POSIXct(
      format(hour_utc, tz = "Asia/Kolkata", usetz = FALSE),
      tz = "Asia/Kolkata"
    ),
    date = as.Date(hour_ist, tz = "Asia/Kolkata")
  ) %>%
  filter(hour_ist >= start_ist, hour_ist < end_ist) ->
  gfs_hourly

gfs_hourly %>%
  summarise(
    hours = n(),
    duplicate_hours = sum(duplicated(hour_utc)),
    missing_rain = sum(is.na(rain_mm)),
    rain_mm = sum(rain_mm)
  )

gfs_hourly %>%
  summarise(gfs_mm = sum(rain_mm), .by = date) ->
  gfs_daily

open_dataset(
  file.path(root_dir, "data", "weatherunion_bengaluru_hourly.parquet")
) %>%
  filter(
    hour_ist >= start_ist,
    hour_ist < end_ist,
    locality_id %in% complete_stations$locality_id
  ) %>%
  collect() %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(hour_ist, tz = "Asia/Kolkata")) %>%
  summarise(
    rain_mm = sum(rain_mm),
    .by = c(locality_id, date)
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    station_median_mm = median(rain_mm),
    station_max_mm = max(rain_mm),
    .by = date
  ) %>%
  inner_join(gfs_daily, by = "date") %>%
  filter(date >= as.Date("2026-09-20"), date <= as.Date("2026-09-21"))
```

The reconstructed GFS series has 648 distinct valid hours and totals
110.76 mm, closer to the complete-station monthly median than the stored
Oikolab total. Its September 21 IST forecast is 66.4 mm, above even the wettest
complete station's 40 mm that day. Monthly agreement does not establish
daily accuracy.

Oikolab describes ERA5 as a roughly 31 km historical reanalysis and GFS as a
forecast model. They are different products. WeatherUnion sensors measure
particular neighbourhoods and currently come from a manually refreshed local
archive. A rainfall display should disclose which of these it uses and its
coverage date. Keep ERA5 rows intact for like-for-like historical analysis.

## Verdict

Insightful: no

The stored Oikolab rain total is much lower than September totals at every complete
WeatherUnion station. A September-only GFS rainfall display is technically
possible using the archived 00Z runs and avoids the large monthly undercount.
It must be labelled as a forecast reconstruction; its September 21 value
overpredicts every complete WeatherUnion station. Apply any exception to the
display layer, preserve ERA5 rows, and exclude the mixed-source September
series from like-for-like records and normals.

This is a data-source repair, not a publishable weather story. The daily chart
and site CSV now use the September GFS override. No blog post was published.

Charts: none.

Blog post: not published.
